key_insight: GFlowQEC learns to propose promising quantum LDPC codes, finding more new top-scoring designs per expensive evaluation than tuned parallel tempering.
engineering_relevance: A pretrained code proposer can stretch limited quantum-code evaluation budgets by prioritizing candidates before costly scoring.
method: Build lifted-product codes one group element at a time using a generative flow network.
Train on earlier search scores to sample codes in proportion to a power of their score, then freeze the model.
Rank batches of proposed codes and spend paid evaluations on selected candidates.
evidence_signal: For distance-scored, 180-physical-qubit codes, ranking 10 draws per paid call found over 2× as many new top-scoring codes as tuned parallel tempering and over 3.5× as many as a supervised screen ranking 10 random candidates.
watch_item: Performance depends on the comparator and screening budget: screening 100 random candidates beat GFlowQEC, while soft Q-learning matched or exceeded it across the two tested noise biases.
paper_title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
